item.title: Products and duality for framed 1-flow categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.31337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe a product between framed 1-flow categories and show that it satisfies the expected Cartan formula on its second Steenrod squares. We also describe a dual framed 1-flow category and show that, like the Spanier-Whitehead dual of spectra, the homology groups of a framed 1-flow category can be shown to be isomorphic to the cohomology groups of its dual and that this isomorphism can be shown to cooperate with the framed 1-flow category structure in a suitable sense.
item.dc:creator: Chris Johnson

item.title: Topological Inference for degree-Cech complexes
item.description: arXiv:2611.31505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study topological inference for the degree-Cech bifiltration from noisy samples of a manifold. Under a model combining uniform sampling on the manifold with uniform noise, we show that suitable choices of the radius and degree parameters recover the homotopy type of the underlying manifold with high probability. The analysis explains how the degree parameter suppresses sufficiently distant outliers while the radius scale captures topological signals. Our results provide theoretical support for the common intuition that degree bifiltrations carry meaningful topological information in the presence of noise.
item.dc:creator: Michael Kerber, Bria Razanaparany

item.title: Characterizing $2$-slices over finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.32512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite group $G$, we characterize the $2$-slices of $G$-spectra in the regular slice filtration in terms of their homotopy Mackey functors and $k$-invariant. We explicitly compute this for cyclic $p$-groups and the alternating group $A_4$.
item.dc:creator: Surojit Ghosh, Ankit Kumar

item.title: One monoid to realize them all: a master monoid for homotopy types
item.description: arXiv:2611.32655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Homotopy theory has traditionally been approached either through topological spaces or through categories of presheaves on suitable combinatorial categories, a perspective subsumed by Grothendieck's theory of test categories. In this paper, we develop a more algebraic viewpoint: homotopy types can be represented by actions of a single monoid on sets. This monoid is obtained by identifying all the objects of the semisimplicial category while retaining its face operators. Every CW homotopy type is the classifying space of the translation category of one of its actions, and its truncation at dimension n is finitely presented and realizes exactly the homotopy types of dimension at most n. The construction rests on a general result: every set-valued functor on a small category freely generates an action of its universal monoid, and its category of elements is a full coreflective subcategory of the resulting translation category. Hence every weak test category gives rise to a monoid whose actions realize all homotopy types; when the category has more than one object, however, this monoid is not itself a weak test category, so that a single monoid may realize all homotopy types without modelling homotopy theory as a localization. The obstruction lies in identifying objects, not in having a single one: there are strict test categories with a single object, such as the monoid of all self-maps of an infinite set and a countable monoid of primitive recursive functions.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Carcac\'ia-Campos

item.title: Twisted $L^2$-torsion functions obstruct fibring over the circle
item.description: arXiv:2611.32771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The vanishing of the L^2-Betti numbers of the universal covering of a closed manifold is an obstruction to fibring over the circle. When the L^2-Betti numbers vanish we introduce a secondary obstruction based on the asymptotic behaviour of the twisted L^2-torsion function at 0 and infinity. We provide a number of examples showing the invariant is indeed non-trivial.
item.dc:creator: Sam Hughes, Wolfgang Lueck

item.title: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.33125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and their compactifications.
item.dc:creator: Coline Emprin, Alex Takeda

item.title: Second homotopy modules and infinite homotopy stable classes of four-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.31642v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct infinitely many closed oriented smooth 4-manifolds which are all stably diffeomorphic but pairwise not homotopy equivalent. Our examples are distinguished by their second homotopy modules, and provide the first examples which demonstrate that stable diffeomorphism does not determine the second homotopy module. They have fundamental group $(\mathbb{Z}/4)^4*\mathbb{Z}$ and arise as doubles of presentation 2-complexes. In contrast, we give criteria for isomorphism of second homotopy modules of doubles of 2-complexes, covering finite abelian, quaternion, dihedral and symmetric fundamental groups. We also establish non-injectivity of the doubling construction by showing that there exist homotopically distinct presentation 2-complexes over $Q_{28}$ whose doubles are homotopy equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Tommy Hofmann, John Nicholson

item.title: Cup products with volume classes in bounded cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2611.32555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $\omega\in \Omega_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$. In the case of closed orientable surfaces, this generalizes a result of Marasco, and, via transfer, provides a new proof of the fact that the cup product of the bounded Euler class of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with itself vanishes. Our result also applies to degree-3 bounded classes constructed by Soma and Farre, thus showing that, for surface groups and for free groups, the annihilator of the cup product is infinite dimensional also in degree 3.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Bucher, Roberto Frigerio

item.title: An internal approach to symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.33107v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a definition of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories as special left double $(\infty,n)$-fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The definition makes sense in a general model of $(\infty,n)$-categories, under a mild condition on its discrete objects, and when the model is left proper and combinatorial we construct model structures whose fibrant objects are exactly these fibrations. For $n=1$ we show that the definition recovers Lurie's symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories: the homotopy theory of special left double $(\infty,1)$-fibrations is equivalent to that of special coCartesian fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The equivalence is realized by an explicit Quillen equivalence, and two constructions, the staircase and coCartesian strings, translate between the two descriptions.
item.dc:creator: Arghan Dutta

item.title: The homotopy types of $Sp(n)$-gauge groups over $S^{4m}$
item.description: arXiv:2204.08867v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $m$ and $n$ be two positive integers such that $m < n$, and let $Q_{n-m+1}$ be the symplectic quasi-projective space of rank $n-m+1$. Denote by $P_{n,k}$ the principal $\mathrm{Sp(n)}$-bundle over $S^{4m}$ and $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(\mathrm{Sp(n)})$ be the gauge group of $P_{n,k}$ classified by $k\varepsilon'$, where $\varepsilon'$ is a generator of $\pi_{4m}(B(\mathrm{Sp(n)}))\cong\mathbb{Z}$. In this article, first, we will study the order of the Samelson product $S^{4m-1}\wedge Q_{n-m+1}\rightarrow \mathrm{Sp(n)}$. Then, by the unstable $K$-theory method, we will partially classify the homotopy types of $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(\mathrm{Sp(n)})$ by giving a lower bound for the number of homotopy types of $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(\mathrm{Sp(n)})$.
item.dc:creator: Sajjad Mohammadi

item.title: On the action of the mapping class group on the fundamental group of a surface
item.description: arXiv:2305.04109v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe the action of the mapping class group $M(g,n)$ on the fundamental group of $S_{g,n}$, the complement of $n$ distinct points in a compact orientable surface of positive genus $g$. This is achieved by computing the image of the generators of $M(g,n)$ as outer automorphisms of the fundamental group.
item.dc:creator: Luca Da Col

item.title: Fast Queries of Fibered Barcodes
item.description: arXiv:2511.05837v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The fibered barcode $\mathcal{F}(M)$ of a bipersistence module $M$ is the map sending each non-negatively sloped affine line $\ell \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ to the barcode of the restriction of $M$ along $\ell$. The simplicity, computability, and stability of $\mathcal{F}(M)$ make it a natural choice of invariant for data analysis applications. In an earlier preprint [arXiv:1512.00180], we introduced a framework for real-time interactive visualization of $\mathcal{F}(M)$, which allows the user to select a single line $\ell$ via a GUI and then plots the associated barcode. This visualization is a key feature of our software RIVET for the visualization and analysis of bipersistent homology. Such interactive visualization requires a framework for efficient queries of $\mathcal{F}(M)$, i.e., for quickly obtaining the barcode along a given line $\ell$. To enable such queries, we introduced a novel data structure based on planar line arrangements, called an augmented arrangement. The aim of the present paper is to give an updated and improved exposition of the parts of our preprint [arXiv:1512.00180] concerning the mathematics of the augmented arrangement and its computation. Notably, by taking the input to be a minimal presentation rather than a chain complex, we are able to substantially simplify our main algorithm and its complexity analysis.
item.dc:creator: Michael Lesnick, Matthew Wright

item.title: Binary Minor Certificates for the $\mathcal A(1)$-hit problem of $MO(2)$
item.description: arXiv:2609.20859v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M=\widetilde H^*(MO(2);\mathbb F_2)$ and let $\mathcal A(1)$ be the subalgebra of the mod $2$ Steenrod algebra generated by $\operatorname{Sq}^1$ and $\operatorname{Sq}^2$. In this work, we determine the quotient $\mathbb F_2\otimes_{\mathcal A(1)}M$ in every internal degree $h\geq0$, where internal degree $h$ corresponds to cohomological degree $h+2$. To overcome the limitations of finite experimental extrapolation, our proof is strictly certifying: in each degree, we exhibit a determinant-one minor of the binary hit matrix and a complementary family of linear dual functionals annihilating every hit column, mathematically guaranteeing the exact rank for all degrees. This rigorously establishes the monomial generating families and module decomposition proposed in Shih's 2012 report. Furthermore, we derive a closed binomial formula for every Steenrod square from the length-two symmetric-polynomial model, correct a boundary omission in the $\mathcal A(0)$ calculation, compute the exact Hilbert series of the $\mathcal A(1)$-cohit, and prove an intrinsic direct-sum decomposition of $M$ into two stable $\mathcal A(1)$-submodules.
item.dc:creator: Dang Vo Phuc

item.title: Formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy
item.description: arXiv:2611.25421v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a connected finite-type CW-complex with a map to the circle that is surjective on fundamental groups. If $X$ is formal, the algebraic monodromy of the associated infinite cyclic cover has no Jordan block of size greater than one at the eigenvalue 1, over the rationals; formality of the $d$-fold cyclic cover rules out such blocks at the $d$-th roots of unity. We study how formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy constrain each other. We call $X$ Alexander formal if there are no such blocks at any root of unity, rationally, nor at the eigenvalue 1 modulo any prime; this is a formality property of cochains, as DG modules over the cohomology of the circle. The complement of a central hyperplane arrangement, with its Milnor fibration, is Alexander formal exactly when the numbers of hyperplanes in its irreducible factors have no common divisor greater than 1. We also show that a CDGA graded by an abelian group, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, is formal if and only if it is formal as a graded CDGA. Hence the strong formality of Kohno and Pajitnov implies formality of every finite abelian cover of $X$, but not conversely. Modulo $p$, eigenvalues of $p$-power order collide with 1, producing Jordan blocks that strong formality allows; the two conditions are incomparable, and all four resulting classes contain arrangement complements.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Suciu

item.title: Homotopy types of complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs and applications to right-angled Artin groups
item.description: arXiv:2503.08411v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we prove that, given two finite connected graphs $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$, if the two right-angled Artin groups $A(\Gamma_1)$ and $A(\Gamma_2)$ are quasi-isometric, then the infinite pointed sums $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} \Gamma_1^{\bowtie}$ and $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} \Gamma_2^{\bowtie}$ are homotopy equivalent, where $\Gamma_i^{\bowtie}$ denotes the simplicial complex whose vertex-set is $\Gamma_i$ and whose simplices are given by joins. These invariants are extracted from a study, of independent interest, of the homotopy types of several complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs (such as one-skeleta of CAT(0) cube complexes). For instance, given a quasi-median graph $X$, the \emph{crossing complex} $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is the simplicial complex whose vertices are the hyperplanes (or $\theta$-classes) of $X$ and whose simplices are collections of pairwise transverse hyperplanes. When $X$ has no cut-vertex, we show that $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is homotopy equivalent to the pointed sum of the links of all the vertices in the prism-completion $X^\square$ of $X$.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Abbott, Anthony Genevois, Eduardo Martinez-Pedroza

item.title: Cospan contexts and higher categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.24473v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by the desire to turn the cobordism hypothesis (a statement about the universal property of some $n$-category of bordisms) into a $1$-categorical statement, we prove that all $n$-categories can be modeled by \emph{$n$-cospan contexts}: these are $1$-categories equipped with a collection of iterated cospans that satisfy a composition property in terms of pushouts. In particular, we construct an adjunction from $\mathsf{Cat}_n$ to the category of $n$-cospan contexts which simultaneously generalizes the $n$-fold span construction of Haugseng and the twisted arrow category construction (when $n = 1$).
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Riva

item.title: Stable compatibility for model categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.00813v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: By introducing the notion of stable compatibility, we provide a framework in the model category theory which addresses the existence of a stable model structure on the category of modules over a monad. Exact version of such monads have been studied in the setting of triangulated categories, separately as separable monads a la Balmer in tensor triangular geometry and non-separable monads a la Dell'Ambrogio and Sanders in stable homotopy theory. By introducing stable compatibility, we explore their properties together and produce a non-separable monad in Algebraic geometry and more.
item.dc:creator: Kunal Arora, Vivek Mohan Mallick

item.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks
item.description: arXiv:2611.17557v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$. If $C_f\to G$ denotes the free crossed module determined by $f$, then the associated crossed modules of $R_f\to G$ and $Q_f\to G$ are both isomorphic to $C_f\to G$. We also characterize free augmented quandles in terms of stabilizers. As applications, we prove that the canonical inner augmentation of every generalized Alexander quandle is free. For a classical knot quandle, the canonical inner augmentation is free if and only if the knot is a torus knot. For every $n$-knot with $n\geq2$, the canonical inner augmentation is also free.
item.dc:creator: Toshiyuki Akita, Sota Takase
